reason: Copper Finch Mechanical sent two overlapping invoices dated 10 Feb, both for the correct address and the assigned firm: A for £138 and B for £372 (invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-A.pdf, invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-B.pdf, event-017, event-018). Invoice A matches the £138 diagnostic quote (event-007) and sits within the landlord's £180 diagnosis-only authority (event-005). Invoice B bills actuator replacement as done on 5 Feb. The landlord never approved that work (event-012), the £372 estimate was only sent after the visit (event-009), and the file has no authorization or completion record (event-019). The tenant does not know whether the actuator was replaced (event-020). The contractor has twice failed to say whether one invoice replaces the other, whether the diagnosis is credited, or whether the work was done (event-016, event-022). The two documents conflict with the history, and the charge is disputed in effect. Policy sends duplicate or suspicious invoices and conflicting versions to a person. A third question to the provider or a further chase would repeat what has already failed. Routing the £372 for approval would be wrong, because the work may not have been done and the landlord has not asked for it. Nothing is payable meanwhile. I set P2, not P0 or P1: the heating works intermittently and hot water is available. There is no gas, leak or smell concern (event-008, event-011). A portable heater is in use and a child lives at the property, which the handover flags. The reference-number flag only reflects the two different invoice suffixes. The landlord has been asked for a decision (event-023). A follow-up is set for 48 hours to check for his reply. This would change if the contractor produces job notes and a parts record, or the landlord gives written direction.
unknowns: Whether the actuator was replaced
Whether invoice B supersedes A
Whether the diagnosis charge is credited
Landlord's decision on the repair and the invoices
options: Hold both invoices until the landlord replies and the contractor provides job notes and a parts record; pay A only on the landlord's confirmation
Dispute invoice B as unauthorized and unevidenced and ask for a single corrected invoice with any credit stated
If the landlord wants the repair, get written approval and a fixed itemised price, then book a return visit with the tenant

actions.summary: Copper Finch Mechanical sent two overlapping invoices dated 10 Feb for 7 Larkspur Fold (A £138, B £372). B bills actuator replacement for 5 Feb, but there is no authorization or completion evidence for that work. Do not pay either invoice until a person has reviewed them. Heating is still intermittent, and a child lives at the property.
known: Landlord authorized diagnosis only, up to £180 incl VAT, and asked to be consulted before any remedial work (event-005, event-012).
Contractor quoted £138 incl VAT for attendance, diagnosis and testing, with parts and remedial work excluded (event-007). Invoice A for £138 matches that quote (invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-A.pdf).

Estimate of £372 for actuator replacement was sent 5 Feb at 14:54, after the visit (event-009). The landlord has not approved it (event-012). Our note records no written authorization and no completion entry (event-019).
Invoice B for £372 describes actuator supply and replacement as done on 5 Feb. It overlaps invoice A's attendance and diagnosis, and no credit is stated (invoice-NBL-CFM-250210-B.pdf, event-018).

On 7 Feb the contractor said parts availability and the estimate details were still being checked (event-016). On 12 Feb she said she could not confirm whether the records are separate chargeable work or whether one replaces the other, and gave no completion evidence (event-022).
The tenant does not know whether the actuator was replaced and has seen no contractor since 5 Feb (event-020). Heating is still intermittent, and hot water is available.
Both invoices carry the correct address and the assigned firm's name. Property and provider match; the problem is the duplication and the missing authority.
We emailed the landlord on 12 Feb at 16:35 for a decision, and there is no reply yet (event-023).

options: Recommended: Hold both invoices. Wait for the landlord's reply and the contractor's job notes and parts record. Consider paying only invoice A (£138), which is within the diagnosis authority, once the landlord confirms.
Dispute invoice B in writing as unauthorized and unevidenced. Ask the contractor for a single corrected invoice, with any credit stated, before any payment.

If the landlord wants the repair done, get a written approval and a fixed, itemised price from the contractor. Book an access-confirmed return visit with the tenant, who can give access after 14:00 on weekdays, to restore the heating.
